title: pcapng: Handle excessively long string option consistently
description:
wiretap/merge.c function create_shb_header() dynamically generates
the string "File created by merging:...". This string is normally
added as a capture file comment to the SHB.

With enough filenames of sufficient lengths the generated string can
exceed the maximum pcapng string option data size of 65535.

If the generated string exceeds 65536 bytes mergecap will generate an
invalid pcapng file. The SHB will contain an invalid block length value
which results in an unusable pcapng file.

In wiretap/pcapng.c the function pcapng_compute_string_option_size()
curiously returns the modulo 65536 value of the strlen() of the string.
This value is ultimately used to calculate the block length. But
wiretap/pcapng.c function pcapng_write_string_option() ultimately
ignores any string option with a strlen() greater than 65535.

This patch updates pcapng_compute_string_option_size() to return a
size of 0 when strlen() exceeds 65535.

Future work should include reviewing all uses of the `size = ... & 0xffff`
idiom; e.g:

   git grep 'size = (uint32_t).*& 0xffff;'

notes.body:
> Future work should include reviewing all uses of the `size = ... & 0xffff` idiom; e.g:

..and doing something better than just refusing to write the option.

The simplest solution is to truncate the strings at 65535 octets.

The simplest *correct* slution is to truncate the strings at 65535 octets *and make sure no partial UTF-8 character is left at the end of the string as a result of the truncation slicing a UTF-8 character in half*.  For example:

* if the string is empty, you're done. Otherwise:
* look at the last octet of the string;
* if the last octet of the string is a '\0', back up to the previous octet, lather, rinse, and repeat until you hit a non-'\0' or are at the beginning of the string;
* if you're at the beginning of the string you're done. Otherwise:
* if the octet you're now looking at has the uppermost bit clear, you're done. Otherwise:
* if the uppermost two bits of the octet are `10`, count this octet, back up to the previous octet, later, rinse, and repeat until you hit an octet in which the upper two bits are not `10` or are at the beginning of the string, and:
* * if you're at the beginning of the string, it's malformed UTF-8, but not as a result of truncation, so you're done. Otherwise:
* * if the uppermost bit of the octet is `0`, it's malformed UTF-8, but not as a result of truncation, so you're done. Otherwise:
* * if the uppermost three bits of the octet are `110`, it's either valid UTF-8 or it's malformed UTF-8, but not as a result of truncation, so you're done. Otherwise:
** if the uppermost four bits of the octet are `1110`, and the count is 1, it's malformed UTF-8 as a result of the truncation, so remove the current octet and the next octet from the string, and you're done, otherwise, it's valid UTF-8, and you're done. Otherwise:
* * if the uppermost five bits of the octet are `11110`, and the count is 1 or 2, it's malformed UTF-8 as a result of the truncation, so remove the current octet and the next "count" octets from the string, and you're done, otherwise, it's valid UTF-8, and you're done. Otherwise:
* * it's not valid UTF-8, but not as a result of truncation, so you're done.
* if the uppermost three bits of the octet are `110, or the uppermost four bits of the octet are `1110`, or the uppermost five bits of the octet are `11110`, then it's malformed UTF-8 as a result of the truncation, so discard the current octet from the string, and you're done; otherwisse, it's malformed UTF-8, but not as a result of the truncation, so you're done.

(See the table in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTF-8#Description.)

For extra credit, you could stick an ellipsis at the end to indicate that truncation was done to the string, but that way lies madness.

As for

> wiretap/merge.c function create_shb_header() dynamically generates the string "File created by merging:...". This string is normally added as a capture file comment to the SHB.

what we really should have is a way, perhaps with additional block and option types, to give a full history of the file, including programs that modified the file or generated new files from the file, but that's a bigger project, and would require pcapng changes.

> The simplest correct slution is to truncate the strings at 65535 octets and make sure no partial UTF-8 character is left at the end of the string as a result of the truncation slicing a UTF-8 character in half.

Libwsutil str_util.h has a `ws_utf8_truncate` function that does this. Note that function assumes that the string is valid UTF-8 before truncation. There are separate functions to verify that the string is valid if necessary.
